40050102.text: Ah, Freminet, you're home. Where did everyone else go? I have some new friends that I would like to introduce.

40050103.text: Oh, they all just went out a moment ago.

40050104.text: I see. Everyone is getting busier now that "Father" will be returning soon. I suppose that can't be helped...

40050105.text: Allow me to introduce you to my little brother, Freminet. He is a phenomenal diver.

40050107.text: #Nice to meet you! Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. You sound very proud to have a diver as a brother, Lyney.

40050111.text: Uh, Lyney... Could you come here for a moment?

40050112.text: Hmm? What is it, Freminet? Do you have something to tell me?

40050116.text: Oh, it's nothing, we were just discussing a little housework. Sorry for the interruption.

40050117.text: #Before I forget, {NICKNAME} and I collected more materials to make Magic Pockets. Were you able to get any, Freminet?

40050118.text: Yes, I went diving and gathered lots of materials. I was about to give them to you.

40050119.text: That's our Freminet, always quick with the underwater work. Alright, I'll take these to the workshop.

40050121.text: Oh, you're right. But wasn't it clear and sunny just a moment ago? Hmm... Fontaine's weather sure is weird.

40050122.text: Hehe, I'm afraid that's just how it is here. It often rains on days when there are trials being held in the opera house, but don't worry, it'll clear up soon enough.

40050125.text: There's a legend about the rain that I tend to believe...

40050126.text: It's said that a Dragon of Water once resided in Fontaine. Though we don't know where the dragon went, every time it weeps, the skies will cloud up and pour out rain.

40050127.text: When I was a child, my mother told me that if I wanted to go outside and play, I should yell toward the sky at the top of my lungs...

40050202.text: Oh, hello there. New customers? Looking to buy, or do you need something made? Or perhaps you're just looking for a chat with me?

40050203.text: Oh — no, we're just here to deliver some materials. Here they are. They're for making... uh, what were they called again?

40050204.text: Ah, these must be for Magic Pockets. I could tell right away, I've already made several orders' worth now.

40050206.text: No, no need. They've already prepaid several batches worth. When they told me what they'd be using them for, I even offered them a discount.

40050207.text: But they insisted on paying the full amount, saying that I had a business to run... Hehe, it seems both their hearts and their pockets are made of gold.

40050208.text: Whoa, so is Lyney actually loaded?

40050209.text: I can't say for sure, but who knows... Maybe there's good money to be made being a magician in Fontaine.

40050210.text: Hey, is this machine what you use to make stuff here? It looks really advanced...

40050211.text: Why use your hands when a machine can do the work? It would be a waste not to use the latest technology, and wasting is a kind of crime.

40050212.text: But where does a big machine like that get its power from?

40050213.text: Ah, well... It's a little complicated, I'm not sure I can put it in layman's terms for you...

40050214.text: But basically, everything we usually use here in the city is powered by Indemnitium. It's a type of energy that's produced from trials.

40050215.text: Huh? How can trials produce energy?

40050216.text: Well, I'm not completely sure of all the details myself, but basically...

40050217.text: When a trial is in session, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale harvests people's belief in justice, and converts it into energy to be used all around Fontaine.

40050218.text: So that's what its other function is? Paimon heard that the Oratrice was created by the Archon to make judgments.

40050219.text: But Paimon still doesn't get it. How could something unreliable like people's beliefs be turned into a stable power source for these machines?

40050222.text: Oh, yeah! So that means the Hydro Archon relies on the machine to take the energy created by belief and turn it into power for all of Fontaine, right?

40050223.text: Even though I've never heard anyone really put it that way before, it sounds like it makes sense.

40050224.text: Besides Indemnitium, we have another type of energy called "Pneumousia."

40050225.text: It isn't produced by the power of the Archon, but it is unstable by nature. Even now it still cannot be widely used by civilians.

40050226.text: Heh, I thought I'd find you hard at work, but here you are chatting the day away... Since you're already talking, I'm sure you wouldn't mind a few words with me.

40050227.text: Y—You again? Didn't I already promise you that I'd have the Mora I owe to Confrerie of Cabriere by next month? Why are you hounding me now?

40050228.text: Yeah, but how do we know that you won't go running off by the end of this month? I want fifty percent. Today. Wait, no... seventy percent.

40050230.text: Seems business isn't so great for the workshop... We've already finished our job and delivered the materials. Maybe now's a good time to leave?

subQuests.subQuestName: Defeat the Confrerie of Cabriere henchmen

40050401.text: What's your deal, brat...? How are you so strong if you're just a staffer from Snezhnaya's Northland Bank? ...Wait, don't tell me you're—!

40050402.text: Oh, now you notice? It's a little late, don't you think? Just make sure you understand that you don't mess with Northland Bank, got it?

40050408.text: I'm not sure... It's as if I suddenly lost control of my Hydro powers when I needed them. Maybe there's something wrong with my Vision?

40050409.text: Strange, how could that happen? First time Paimon's ever heard of someone losing control of their Vision.

40050410.text: Never mind, it doesn't matter. If I wanna stay sharp, I shouldn't be relying too much on my Vision anyway. Besides, I always have my Delusion in case I need it.

40050501.text: Wow, who could have seen that coming!? The reporter who was barely around for most of the story was the murderer all along!

40050504.text: Ah, sorry... Paimon was just surprised, that's all. Whew, Paimon never saw that twist coming... The murder mystery novels here are amazing!

subQuests.subQuestName: Ride the Navia Line and head to Erinnyes
Ride the Navia Line and head to Erinnyes
Go to the fountain plaza in front of the opera house

40050901.text: Whoa, now this is fancy! The Opera Epiclese... What a place to hold a performance, no wonder Lyney and Lynette were looking forward to it.

40050902.text: Huh? Looks like there's a lot of people standing around the fountain up ahead.

40050903.text: O Archon... please bless us with a bright and healthy child. We pray—

40050904.text: ...I don't know why you always feel the need to ask so much... I'll be happy as long as our child is healthy, and lives a peaceful life.

40050905.text: Hehe, I guess if they're our kid, then there's no doubt they'll turn out smart.

40050906.text: Maybe this is one of the customs in Fontaine? There sure are a lot of couples here...

40050911.text: Did you just say something, Paimon?

40050912.text: No, Paimon didn't say anything. Are you hearing things?

40050915.text: Welcome to the Fountain of Lucine. All the water flowing through Fontaine converges here. It's customary for newlyweds to come here and wish for children.

40050916.text: Waah! Lynette! You scared Paimon! When did you get here?

40050917.text: Lyney asked me to wait here for you, remember?

40051001.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, good to see you. I knew you two would come.

40051002.text: Are you kidding? We wouldn't miss it for the world. We've been looking forward to it!

40051003.text: Hehe. I can tell, judging by how early you've arrived.

40051004.text: But you're actually right on time. The audience still hasn't started entering the venue yet, which means now is the perfect chance for us to take you to the best seats in the house. Wait just a moment, I'll fetch the tickets.

40051005.text: The opera house has assigned seating, so you always have to make reservations. I've already reserved your seats, and here are your tickets.

40051006.text: Ooh! Front row seats! Thanks, Lyney!

40051007.text: Don't mention it, there's no need to keep thanking me...

40051008.text: Hey, Lyney! Could you come over here and take a look at this?

40051009.text: Oh, I'll be right there. Seems there's an issue with the stage props over there. That's Cowell, my assistant, calling me. I'll go lend him a hand.

40051012.text: Yeah, we'll just go to our seats. You go ahead, Lyney.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the seats Lyney arranged

40053001.text: Ooh, these should be our seats. C'mon, let's sit down.

40053007.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}... Maybe we should strike up a conversation with the person next to us? Since we're sitting together and the rest of the place is practically empty still, it's kinda awkward if we don't say anything.

40053010.text: You little... Of course you put this on Paimon...

40053011.text: Excuse me, I did not realize you felt awkward. I am terribly sorry.

40053012.text: I would be perfectly happy to chat with you if that's what you would like.

40053013.text: Oh... uh... So you heard all of that, did ya? Boy, you sure have good ears, Paimon thought she was keeping her voice down.

40053014.text: Ah! Wait, that's not it, Paimon's sorry! Um, Paimon's the one who was being rude talking under her breath like that. Uh, so let's talk, but... uh... what should we talk about?

40053016.text: Uh... Oh, Paimon's got it! You're also here early and sitting in the front. Are you a friend of Lyney's, too?

40053017.text: A... friend, you say? Well, if Mr. Lyney would like to be my friend, I would be more than happy to reciprocate.

40053018.text: Oh, so you're not friends with Lyney, then... Whew, this is getting more awkward by the second. Ah, Paimon nearly forgot to make our introduction...

40053019.text: #Nice to meet you, Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. We just arrived in Fontaine.

40053020.text: It is an honor to meet you two. I have heard of your deeds across Teyvat.

40053021.text: And as required by proper etiquette, I will also introduce myself. I am...

40053022.text: Oh, Monsieur Neuvillette! What an honor it is to have you here to see my show!

40053023.text: Ah, Mr. Lyney. I should say it is in fact an honor for me to see your performance in person.

40053025.text: Hmm? I saw you all chatting just now, but it seems you still don't know who Monsieur Neuvillette is.

40053026.text: Allow me to introduce you to Fontaine's Chief J{RUBY#[S]Iudex}ustice. That seat is always reserved for him. It wouldn't be too much to say that he's the symbol of justice and honesty here in Fontaine.

40053027.text: Whoa! Sorry for being so rude just now. Paimon had no idea you were such an important person...

40053028.text: No offense taken. Being Chief J{RUBY#[S]Iudex}ustice is merely what I do for work. Nearly every person has their usual reserved seat, so I am not so special, really.

40053029.text: And by the way, I should probably let you know, even though I would prefer not to...

40053030.text: There's someone sitting up there in the VIP seats that has been striking a pose for quite a while now...

40053031.text: I believe she's trying to give you a most elegant and impressive first impression.

40053032.text: So I think you should take notice of her sooner rather than later, otherwise she may become flustered.

40053034.text: Huh? Oh, it's Furina, the Hydro Archon. She sure has a smug and satisfied look on her face. Guess she has no idea that you saw right through her act.

40053035.text: Very good, that is for the best. No need to pay her any more attention, we may now enjoy the show.

40053036.text: Huh, so is this what things are like between the Chief Justice and the Hydro Archon?

40053037.text: Alright, please wait just a moment longer. I've pretty much finished my preparations and the performance will start as soon as the audience has made their way to their seats.

40053038.text: Yay, the show's finally about to start. Ooh, Paimon can hardly wait! Paimon's never seen a real live magic show before!

40053039.text: The crowds enter the venue, and the curtains open for the show to begin...

40053040.text: Oh! They're dimming the lights, the show must be starting!

40053042.text: Ah... sorry. Paimon will try to stay quiet, hehe.

40053043.text: Welcome, one and all, to the Opera Epiclese! I am the star of today's show, Lyney!

40053044.text: And over here is my sister, Lynette, who will be working as my wonderful assistant. Please, let's give her a warm welcome!

40053046.text: Haha, I know she may seem to be a little sleepy right now, but that's just a sign that she's nervous.

40053048.text: Now, some of you may be thinking: Two Vision holders who can freely manipulate elemental powers performing magic is not true magic at all.

40053049.text: So, I would like to take a moment to assure you that elemental powers will have nothing to do with what you will witness on the stage today.

40053050.text: Both Lynette and myself have removed our Visions for the show. That way, even the gods won't be able to help us.

40053051.text: Oh, good point. That's what makes the show real magic!

40053052.text: Now, without further ado, let the show begin! Lynette will now exit the stage to make some preparations.

40053053.text: I know you might miss her, but don't worry, she'll be coming right back on stage momentarily... Perhaps in an unexpected way. I'm sure she'll be stealing the spotlight soon enough.

40053054.text: Oh, and before I forget... There's one more thing I should say.

40053055.text: You never know what can happen in the blink of an eye.

40051601.text: Whoa! What in the world just happened!? How did he do that!? Paimon didn't see him do anything!

40051602.text: Wasn't Lynette inside the water tank? How did she disappear and then reappear out of nowhere!?

40051605.text: If we could see easily through his tricks, then that would mean that his skills are still lacking.

40051606.text: To appreciate magic, you should focus on the show happening on stage rather than getting caught up in trying to see that which has been intentionally hidden.

40051607.text: Ah, guess you're right. Paimon couldn't believe her eyes when Lynette reappeared. Amazing!

40051608.text: Thank you, thank you, everyone. I'm glad you enjoyed that performance...

40051609.text: But our magical journey has only just begun. I've prepared even more astonishing surprises for everyone here.

40051610.text: The magic of transformation and disappearance can go far beyond what you've just seen.

40051611.text: I'm sure many of you are thinking that escaping the water tank was impressive enough, but Lynette is still my assistant, after all.

40051612.text: In which case, I have ample time to make all necessary preparations.

40051613.text: So for my next trick, I will require the participation of one lucky audience member.

40051614.text: Please, if my assistants could bring out the magical boxes now...

40051615.text: There are two boxes, and only two boxes. One is here, and one is there in the aisle among the audience.

40051616.text: I'm sure many of our clever audience members have already guessed our next magic trick. A swap!

40051617.text: Our lucky audience member and I will each enter a magic box. After one minute, we will each emerge from the opposite box.

40051618.text: Now please, everyone pay very close attention to the box you see here. Don't give me any chance to make a move!

40051619.text: Wow! How's he gonna do this?

40051620.text: Hey, do you think this is all magic tricks, or does Lyney have actual superpowers?

40051202.text: Is this... part of the show?

40051203.text: Mr. Lyney, you're going to use magic to fix the stage now, right?

40051205.text: Oh no, maybe this isn't part of the show... The girl was still in that box, right?

40051206.text: This performance is over! Medical staff, with me. Gardes, secure the scene and detain all the performers. Seal the exits, no one is allowed in or out at this time!

40051207.text: Yes, th—that's right! If this was just an accident, then we must investigate the cause. But if this was all part of some scheme, then... then those accountable will not escape the judgment of the God of Justice!

40051208.text: No need to be alarmed, you two. We'll get to the bottom of this soon enough.

40051209.text: After some time, the Gardes complete their investigation.

40051210.text: Unfortunately, the person who was in the magic box has been pronounced dead. His name was Cowell, one of the assistants in Lyney's magic troupe.

40051211.text: Apparently, the fireworks on stage ignited the ropes that were suspending the water tank, which then caused the tank to fall onto the stage.

40051212.text: As of now, we are still not sure why we found Cowell in the box rather than the guest from the audience.

40051213.text: And after an initial search of the area, the Gardes have confirmed that the girl is nowhere to be found.

40051214.text: It appears that this incident was not merely some mishap with the performance.

40051215.text: And there are many indications that it is connected with the case of the serial disappearances of young women.

40051217.text: Ah, that's the case that Charlotte mentioned before!

40051220.text: Hehe. I know, I know the truth! I can see through the whole thing... Really, using such a shallow and obvious mystery as his "finale"... Did he really underestimate us that badly?

40051221.text: I say that our powerful magician, Mr. Lyney, is now the prime suspect for the serial disappearances case.

40051222.text: Huh, why me? This whole thing was an accident!

40051223.text: This all occurred during your magic show, did it not? The missing girl disappeared after being chosen, did she not? The deceased is one of your assistants, is he not?

40051224.text: Now that I think about it, that whole speech about magicians making things disappear was nothing more than a provocation, a bald-faced challenge!

40051225.text: That can't be right... How could Lyney do this?

40051226.text: He was in the box on stage the entire time. We could even hear his voice.

40051227.text: Besides, before the show he told us that he would like to catch the criminal behind the disappearances. He couldn't possibly mean catching himself!

40054001.text: Thanks again, you two. I really can't deal with that lady...

40059901.text: Under Paimon's enthusiastic leadership, you walk all around the Court of Fontaine...

40059902.text: Lyney said that the opera house is on Erinnyes, so let's go ride the aquabus!
